Phases 3 and 4 · Assessment reference

Assessment & Submission

Phase 3 submits the Excel portfolio analysis. Phase 4 presents and defends the integrated recommendation.

Canvas is the submission authority

Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission mechanics, and course-grade weights. Use the Investment Project Submission rubric for the Phase 3 Excel workbook and the Investment Project Presentation rubric for the Phase 4 integrated oral presentation and defense.

Investment Project Submission rubric · 100 points

Phase 3 Excel workbook

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Evidence quality & technical accuracy20%The provided Reference data, source dates, three class adjustments, category-specific expected and downside returns, covariance/correlation and annualization are used accurately and interpreted. Category total returns include income; security histories estimate price-return risk. A class shift changes the mean while reference SD remains unchanged.
Focused security selection20%Each client has 10 distinct securities with positive final weights, correct class and sector/category classifications, and explicit client-role rationale. The selected category determines its historical baseline; the common Equity, Bond or Cash change supplies the adjustment. Research supports fit, costs, liquidity, overlap and concentration decisions.
Client suitability & IPS compliance15%Each recommendation traces to the client IPS and relevant RRTTLLLU objectives and constraints. Return goals, allocation limits, liquidity, suitability and downside tripwires are checked and explained.
Shared portfolio quality & risk response25%Initial, Solver and final weights are retained and total 100%. Client-specific covariance matrices, Solver constraints and outcomes, final judgment, stress results, corrections and monitoring triggers form one internally consistent portfolio decision.
Individual role evidence & decision trail20%Summary identifies each member contribution. Workbook explanations document the initial judgment, Solver result, final recommendation, rejected alternative, key trade-off, verification and unresolved reservations. No separate Phase 3 Decision Record is required.

Investment Project Presentation rubric · 100 points

Phase 4 live committee presentation and defense

Bring the semester together

Connect the economic review, client IPS statements, security research and Phase 3 workbook in one oral presentation. Each student must explain their contribution, evidence, an alternative rejected, a key trade-off and the integrated portfolio decision.

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Role-specific committee defense25%Within the presentation's compact investment-committee defense, each member answers targeted questions for their role, uses relevant evidence and calculations, acknowledges uncertainty, and defends or revises the judgment under challenge.
Individual evidence & workbook contribution20%Each member demonstrates command of owned evidence and can explain their recommendation, alternative rejected, key trade-off, workbook contribution, verification, and limitations.
Shared portfolio quality & integration25%The committee presents one coherent chain from client scenario analysis through the 10-security-per-client selection, final weights, overlap/concentration decisions, stress results, residual-risk conclusion, correction, and final recommendation.
Client suitability & risk compliance20%Members can show where client needs changed the portfolio, explain the strongest bear case and residual risk, and defend compliance, corrective action, and the residual-risk conclusion.
Clarity, professionalism & visual evidence10%The team communicates concisely as client-focused professionals and uses legible exhibits that make the recommendation, trade-offs, and evidence visible.

Live defense question bank

Prepare to defend owned work and the integrated decision

The panel may direct any question to any member. Role ownership determines preparation responsibility, not permission to ignore the rest of the portfolio.

Client and Macro Strategist

  • Which Phase 1 client fact or guardrail most changed the final portfolio, and where can the committee see that change?
  • Which macro assumption matters most to this recommendation, and what evidence would cause the team to revise it?
  • Which unresolved client information gap remains material, and how did the portfolio avoid pretending it was known?

Fixed-Income Analyst

  • Why does the selected fixed-income exposure fit the client's cash-flow horizon better than the strongest alternative?
  • What happens to price and income if rates or credit spreads move against the position, and which duration or credit evidence supports that answer?
  • What did the Holding & Exposure Reality Check reveal about concentration, liquidity, costs, key risk, and the allocation implication for the selected fixed-income exposure?

Equity Analyst

  • Why does the selected equity fund or ETF deliver the needed exposure better than the strongest alternative after costs, liquidity, overlap, and style or sector concentration?
  • If the portfolio includes an individual equity, why is it superior to a fund or ETF for that role, what is its idiosyncratic risk, and why is the position size appropriate?
  • Which equity candidate did you reject, and what key trade-off separated it from your recommendation?

Portfolio Manager

  • Which analyst recommendations did you integrate, resize, or reject, and what explicit portfolio trade-off drove each decision?
  • Where did you resolve overlap or concentration, and why are the final 10 holdings and weights better than the strongest alternative mix?
  • If the committee rejects one proposed adjustment, what alternative preserves the client goal and what new trade-off does it create?

Risk and Derivatives Analyst

  • Which residual risk contributes most to the bear-case loss, and which client goal is therefore most exposed?
  • Why is the supported conclusion hedge or no hedge, and what evidence makes that conclusion preferable to changing the underlying holdings or weights?
  • If a hedge is proposed, explain the instrument, size, cost, liquidity, trade-offs, residual risk, and adjustment or removal condition.

Any committee member

  • What was the team's strongest initial judgment that changed after AI challenge and human verification?
  • Which FactSet retrieval most affected the recommendation, how did you interpret it, and where is the licensed-source evidence retained under course policy?
  • Which source or calculation carries the most decision weight, and what are its limitations?
  • What is the strongest reasonable case against the final recommendation?
  • What monitoring trigger would force the committee to reconvene before the normal review date?

Final readiness check

Before the committee meeting

  • Each client has 10 distinct positive-weight holdings linked to the IPS, its sector/category historical baseline and the shared Equity, Bond and Cash adjustments.
  • Histories, sources, covariance/correlation matrices and statistics are complete with formulas preserved.
  • Initial, Solver and final allocations are retained; constraints, Solver messages, risk and trade-offs are explained.
  • Summary includes client decisions and team contributions; the single XLSX upload is checked in Canvas.
  • Slides match the final Phase 3 workbook and identify sources and assumptions.
  • Each of the three client recommendations follows from the economic outlook, IPS, research and risk analysis.
  • Every member can explain their contribution and defend the integrated recommendation.
  • The team has checked the Canvas upload and is ready for the oral presentation.

Q&A standard

Every member must be able to defend the market view, mandate, allocation, security choices, stress test, and trade-offs. The panel may direct a question to a member who did not lead that workstream.
